title: Research: inverse-column cut forces R439 frame-508 source to rank four
body:
## Result

This is a scoped exact obstruction for the exceptional R439 phase-B frame 508 source. For the pinned 11-wire map, register 19 must visit the full rank-four block frame under any monotone same-wire XOR circuit whose operation frames stay inside that frame. The proof allows arbitrary circuit length and proper intermediate frames; it extends the predecessor's source-star-prefix obstruction.

The exact inverse column has support `{19, 35, 66, 89, 97, 466}`. Register 466 enters at the full frame. A cut/factorization argument shows that if register 19 never reached that frame, the inverse-column support would have to lie among wires entering in a proper low subframe, a contradiction. The other ten rows already force full-frame exits by dependency span.

Therefore the current direct block climbs remain moment-minimal for (q=1-a\in(0,1)). No new selected κ or supplier adoption is claimed; the selected complex supplier remains unchanged.

## Pins and reproduction

Base commit: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`  
Selected-record SHA-256: `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`  
Cycle seed: `3b2676afb1d8667edc131585f741d4b0`

Run:

```sh
python3 -B research/r439-bsection-stars-seed01/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/r439-frame508-inverse-cut-seed3b/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/r439-frame508-inverse-cut-seed3b/test_verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/r439-frame508-inverse-cut-seed3b --check-only
```

The scalar positive control passes. The exact verifier emits `PASS_R439_FRAME508_INVERSE_CUT`; all five controls pass. Package metadata and pins pass. Direct replay ran with Python 3.14.7. The registered package replay requests Python 3.12, which is unavailable in this environment.

## Scope and attribution

This covers only the exact 11-wire frame-508 matrix with monotone frames inside its rank-four block frame. Added wires, COPY/ERASE, cross-block changes, frames outside the block, native/hosted admission, all-size realization, precision/tape, and analytic-transfer obligations remain open. Frame 509/source 22 remains a separate question.

The predecessor `research/r439-bblock-frame-barrier` settles eight blocks and leaves source 19/22 open; its simple source-star-prefix check does not contain this arbitrary proper-frame cut argument. Credit the R439 lineage: DreamingOfClouds (PR589), eumemic (PR555/543), Sricharan Vagvala (PR967), Aaron Wang (PR1015), Ross Richardson (PR923), and Arham Tahir's frame-barrier work. Prepared by OpenAI Codex with substantial Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review.
